entries.clue: Bit of fennel on outstanding dish (6)

indicatorNotes.Bit of: A bit of a word is a piece off the front of it, and the smallest such piece is its opening letter.

blocks.note: the opening letter of fennel
the word on is taken for its own two letters
a bill still outstanding is due

annotation.surface: A shred of fennel sitting on top of a remarkable dish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' is praise in the surface and unpaid in the wordplay, the sense a bank statement uses. Melted cheese in a communal pot, dipped at with long forks, is the Swiss supper the definition points to.
annotation.definitionFit: A fondue is a dish in its own right, the pot of melted cheese or hot oil a table shares.

entries.clue: Police force briefly ban Miles' organic processes (10)

annotation.definitionNote: Metabolism is a mass noun covering the whole set of chemical processes that keep a body going, so a plural definition answers a singular word.

indicatorNotes.briefly: Something put briefly is cut short, and the word cut short gives up its last letter.

blocks.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
to ban is to abolish, docked of its final H
m = miles, as on a road sign

annotation.surface: The police slapping a short-lived ban on something belonging to Miles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Miles' reads as a first name — Davis, perhaps — and is the road-sign abbreviation. The apostrophe earns nothing but the surface's grammar.
annotation.definitionFit: Metabolism is the sum of the chemical reactions by which a living body builds tissue and burns fuel.

entries.clue: Overtures of moggy's emission of wailing call (4)

indicatorNotes.Overtures of: An overture is what comes first, so each word hands over its opening letter.

blocks.note: the first letters of Moggy's Emission Of Wailing, taken in order

annotation.surface: A cat striking up its nightly wailing.
annotation.walkthrough: A moggy is British for an ordinary unpedigreed cat, so the surface does nothing but describe one. 'Overtures' passes as musical, which is what keeps the initials out of sight.
annotation.definitionFit: A meow is the cry a cat announces itself with, and call covers any animal's characteristic noise.

entries.clue: Sacred texts in animated movie promos cut by Kapoor (10)

indicatorNotes.cut by: A cut opens a gap, and whatever does the cutting ends up sitting in that gap.

blocks.note: Up is the Pixar animation
Anish Kapoor, the British-Indian sculptor
promos are ads

annotation.surface: Trailers for a cartoon film, edited down by somebody called Kapoor.
annotation.walkthrough: The Kapoor the surface suggests is one of Bollywood's; the one the clue wants made Chicago's mirrored Bean. 'Cut by' sounds like editing and asks for an insertion.
annotation.definitionFit: The Upanishads are the philosophical texts that close the Vedas, scripture at the root of Hindu thought.

entries.clue: Worry comedian Phil's doing a head-stand (4)

indicatorNotes.doing a head-stand: A head-stand turns you upside down, and in a down clue that means reading the letters bottom to top.

blocks.note: Phil Wang is a British stand-up, and his surname upended climbs the grid

annotation.surface: Anxiety about the comedian Phil standing on his head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Worry' looks like the mood of the sentence and is the definition, wanting the sense a dog has with a bone. A surname is the whole of the wordplay once it is upended.
annotation.definitionFit: To gnaw at someone is to worry them the way a dog worries a bone — the verb covers both the teeth and the nagging.

entries.clue: Preferred Basset to ring a very old university (8)

indicatorNotes.to ring: To ring something is to draw a circle round it, so these letters close round what follows.

blocks.note: Fred Basset is the hound of the long-running British newspaper strip
the word a, taken as itself
v = very
o = old
u = university

annotation.surface: Choosing a Basset over telephoning some ancient university.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ring' is the telephone in the surface and an enclosure in the wordplay, while 'Basset' passes for a surname and names a breed. The dog has been in the papers since 1963.
annotation.definitionFit: To be favoured is to be preferred, picked out ahead of the alternatives.

entries.clue: Troubled by pitch of note and fade-out (4-4)

indicatorNotes.out: Letters described as out are out of order, no longer in the arrangement they arrived in.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eight letters with 'and' joining the two words
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A sound engineer bothered by the pitch of a note and by a fade-out.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram instruction hides in the tail of a hyphenated word the surface needs whole. Each half of the answer happens to use up one fodder word, which is chance rather than design.
annotation.definitionFit: Somebody tone-deaf cannot hear one pitch as different from another, so pitch is exactly what gives them trouble.

entries.clue: Ridiculous poser dials oaf in happy state of ignorance (5,8)

indicatorNotes.Ridiculous: Something ridiculous is in no sensible state, and neither are these letters until they are sorted.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, thirteen letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: An absurd show-off ringing up an idiot.
annotation.walkthrough: Thirteen letters spread over three short words are easier to spot as fodder than to sort, so count them against the enumeration first. 'Ridiculous' does the shuffling while reading as an opinion of the poser.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone in a fool's paradise is perfectly content only because they do not know what is really going on.

entries.clue: Short rocker shot in land of five rivers (6)

indicatorNotes.Short: A word made short is docked of its last letter.

blocks.note: a punk is a rocker, shortened by a letter
a jab is a shot in the injection sense

annotation.surface: A quick photograph of a rock musician.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' is the camera in the surface and the needle in the wordplay. The definition is a translation rather than a synonym: panj ab is Persian for five waters.
annotation.definitionFit: Punjab is named from the five rivers of the Indus system that cross it, which is what its Persian name says.

entries.clue: Dame from down under embraced by returning wanderer (4)

indicatorNotes.embraced by: An embrace holds something inside it, so these letters sit within the word that follows.
indicatorNotes.returning: Something returning comes back the way it went, so the letters are read in the opposite direction.

blocks.note: wANDErer carries ANDE, and the four letters are read backwards

annotation.surface: An Australian dame in the arms of a traveller coming home.
annotation.walkthrough: The Dame is Barry Humphries' gladioli-waving Melbourne housewife, played on British television for half a century. A hidden run that also reverses is the pairing to look for whenever an enclosing word sits beside a turning one.
annotation.definitionFit: Dame Edna Everage is Barry Humphries' Australian megastar housewife, so the Dame from down under goes by that first name.

entries.clue: See 19
Recollections of Amber Moon raised so regularly (8)

indicatorNotes.regularly: Letters taken regularly come at a fixed interval, and here it is every second one, beginning with the second.

blocks.note: the second letter of AMBER MOON RAISED SO and every other one after it, the count running straight across the spaces

annotation.surface: Somebody called Amber Moon whose name keeps being brought up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raised' offers itself as a reversal instruction and is simply one of the four words being combed. The count starts on the second letter, which is the harder of the two alternate-letter runs to see.
annotation.definitionFit: Memories are what recollection brings back, the individual scenes a mind has kept.

entries.clue: Wayward prisoner locked up by Mo (10)

indicatorNotes.locked up by: Being locked up by somebody puts you inside, with their letters shut round you.

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, an instant
a con is a convict

annotation.surface: An unruly prisoner banged up by a warder called Mo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mo' passes for a name and is the slangy half-minute. The prisoner genuinely does go inside, which is the kind of surface that keeps a container out of sight.
annotation.definitionFit: Somebody inconstant will not hold to one course or one affection, which is the changeable sense of wayward.

entries.clue: Cabbage stuffed with right herb (6)

indicatorNotes.stuffed with: Stuffing goes inside, so the letters that follow are packed into the word before.

blocks.note: a savoy is the crinkle-leaved winter cabbage
r = right

annotation.surface: A cabbage stuffed with exactly the right herb.
annotation.walkthrough: Both halves of the clue sit in the kitchen, so nothing announces where the definition begins. The cabbage and the London hotel take their name from the old Alpine duchy of Savoy.
annotation.definitionFit: Savory is a peppery herb of the mint family, the summer and winter kinds both used in cooking.

entries.clue: Lovely twirling dance competition, on the beach perhaps (10)

indicatorNotes.twirling: Something twirling spins and comes to rest with its parts in a different arrangement.

blocks.note: the six letters of lovely, re-set
a ball is a formal dance

annotation.surface: A lovely spin at a dance contest held on the sand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dance' is the only word doing honest work for the wordplay while staying inside the surface's picture. The beach version, two players a side on sand, has been an Olympic sport since 1996.
annotation.definitionFit: Volleyball is a two-team game played for points, and the beach form is its best-known outdoor version.

entries.clue: Lecturer punches excellent boxer (3)

indicatorNotes.punches: A punch drives in, so the letter throwing it lands inside.

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, and its 1 is written as the letter I
l = lecturer

annotation.surface: A lecturer landing a punch on a first-rate boxer.
annotation.walkthrough: A1 for excellent comes from Lloyd's old grading of ships, and crosswords write its 1 as an I. 'Punches' does the inserting while reading as pure boxing.
annotation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali was the heavyweight champion of the 1960s and 70s, the boxer a three-letter answer nearly always wants.

entries.clue: By empty hall, reference back-flipping Sporty (8)

indicatorNotes.empty: A word emptied keeps only the letters at its two ends; everything between them is gone.
indicatorNotes.back-flipping: A back-flip lands you facing the way you came, so the letters are read in reverse.

blocks.note: at = by, as in sitting at the window
HALL with its middle gone leaves H and L
to reference is to cite, and those four letters are turned round

annotation.surface: Standing by a deserted hall, a mention of Sporty Spice turning back-flips.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sporty' carries a capital because the surface wants the Spice Girl, while the definition needs the plain adjective. An emptied four-letter hall still hands over two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An athletic person is built and moves like a sportsperson, which is what calling somebody sporty claims.

entries.clue: Schumann who scored with Charlie Croft? (5)

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the radio alphabet
Lara Croft, the Tomb Raider heroine

annotation.surface: A Schumann who got lucky with somebody called Charlie Croft.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scored' is the joke: the surface means a conquest, the definition means writing music. The Schumann meant is Robert's wife, a touring virtuoso who composed as well and outlived him by forty years.
annotation.definitionFit: Clara Schumann was a concert pianist and composer in her own right, so she is the Schumann who wrote scores.

entries.clue: Light was at the front (3)

blocks.note: the light-emitting diode that glows in every gadget, known by its three initials
whoever was at the front of the field had the lead

annotation.surface: A lamp mounted at the front of the machine.
annotation.walkthrough: Five words with no seam showing: the same three letters are an acronym read as a noun and an ordinary past tense. Diodes replaced filament bulbs on dashboards and bicycles alike.
annotation.definitionFit: An LED is a light in the everyday sense of the word, and to have led is to have been out in front.

entries.clue: Film of how hunk came to own meth supply (3,3,3,4,3,4)

annotation.answer: THE MAN WHO KNEW TOO MUCH

indicatorNotes.supply: Read as the adverb from supple, not the noun: letters handled supply bend into another shape.

anagram.fodder: HOW HUNK CAME TO OWN METH

blocks.clueFragment: how hunk came to own meth
blocks.note: anagram fodder, twenty letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: How a hunk came by his own supply of methamphetamine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is the trap: it reads as the drug stash the sentence is building towards, and it is an adverb meaning pliantly. Hitchcock shot this title twice, in 1934 and again in 1956.
annotation.definitionFit: The Man Who Knew Too Much is a Hitchcock thriller, made in Britain in 1934 and remade by him in Hollywood in 1956.

entries.clue: Came back with plans we redrafted somewhat (8)

indicatorNotes.somewhat: Somewhat means partly, so only a run of what is written is taken.

blocks.note: the letters lie unbroken in plANS WE REDrafted, running across both spaces

annotation.surface: Plans of ours came back after a partial rewrite.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Redrafted' offers itself as an anagram instruction, which is what buries the run of letters lying right beside it. A hidden answer spanning three words is the hardest kind to notice.
annotation.definitionFit: To come back with a remark is to answer it, the idiom of 'he came back with a flat no'.

entries.clue: European flower festival (6)

blocks.note: e = European
the aster is a daisy-like garden flower

annotation.surface: A festival of European flowers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flower' in crosswords is as often a river, something that flows, as a bloom, and here it really is the garden plant. Aster is Greek for star, which is the shape of its petals.
annotation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival of the Resurrection, the movable feast the church year is built around.

entries.clue: Giving the nod to hairdo: "appropriate, but not feminine" (10)

indicatorNotes.but not: 'But not' excludes what comes after it, so that letter is dropped from the word before.

blocks.note: a perm is a hairdo, short for permanent wave
appropriate = fitting, the word a letter is about to leave
f = feminine, the letter taken out

annotation.surface: A verdict passed on a hairdo: suitable, if not exactly feminine.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make the last three words sound like a stylist's verdict, hiding an instruction to cut a letter. A perm sets curls chemically, which is why it is permanent enough to be named for it.
annotation.definitionFit: Giving the nod to a plan is permitting it, consent signalled by the gesture rather than spoken.

entries.clue: See 19
Wondrous stare from good monkey (4)

blocks.note: g = good
an ape stands in for monkey in the loose everyday sense

annotation.surface: A look of amazement from a well-behaved monkey.
annotation.walkthrough: Apes are not monkeys to a zoologist, and setters swap the words freely. The definition wants a noun, the open-mouthed look itself rather than the act of giving it.
annotation.definitionFit: A gape is the open-mouthed stare you give something astonishing, with the wonder showing on the face.

entries.clue: First, play the part of Simon Templar? (4)

blocks.note: to play the part of someone on stage is to be them
Templar's nickname is the Saint, and saint is written short as st

annotation.surface: A casting note: to begin with, play Simon Templar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First' opens the clue as though it were the order of business, and it is the definition. Leslie Charteris's Templar was the gentleman crook televised as The Saint with Roger Moore in the part.
annotation.definitionFit: Coming first and being best are the same placing, which is why the first prize goes to the best entry.

entries.clue: Mineral in climate control system that's initially adjusted to opposite extreme (6)

indicators: that's initially adjusted to opposite extreme

indicatorNotes.that's initially adjusted to opposite ex: The opening letter is moved to the far end of the alphabet, so an A becomes the letter that finishes it.

blocks.note: air con is the everyday short form of air conditioning

annotation.surface: An air-conditioning unit reset from one temperature extreme to the other.
annotation.walkthrough: The climate surface makes 'opposite extreme' sound like a thermostat swinging from cold to hot when it means the far end of the alphabet. Air con is the British name for the unit.
annotation.definitionFit: Zircon is zirconium silicate, a hard crystalline mineral cut as a gemstone and used to date the oldest rocks.

entries.clue: One ejecting vocal person now saying "t-w-i-t-t-e-r" seven times faster? (8)

indicatorNotes.vocal: A vocal version is the one you hear, so what counts is how the phrase sounds rather than how it is spelt.

blocks.clueFragment: person now saying "t-w-i-t-t-e-r" seven times faster?
blocks.note: somebody spelling a name out is a speller, and since Twitter was renamed X they now spell one letter where there were seven

annotation.surface: A bouncer throwing out a loud type who spells the website's old name aloud.
annotation.walkthrough: Twitter became X in 2023, so spelling the name out dropped from seven letters to one. 'Vocal' passes as a description of the person being thrown out and is the homophone instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: To expel a pupil or a member is to throw them out, so one who expels is one ejecting.
